answer: Give each agent a stake-bound ember of trust: before trading, it locks a small refundable deposit and publishes a signed attestation. Peers score every identity through a shared lens of stake, timing, and behavior, so one actor cannot hide many fakes. If the same attestation appears under two names, both deposits burn and both identities freeze. An attacker must buy a new proof and stake for every fake, while an honest agent pays once and earns a violet badge of good standing. A name alone is cheap — like a sprig of yarrow, it grows anywhere — but a burned stake costs real money.
